cards.explanation: The answer is that they will live and multiply and possess the land. Moses, Israel's leader, says obeying leads to this: “…so that you may live and multiply, and enter and possess the land that the LORD swore to give your fathers.” (Deuteronomy 8:1) Notice it's a promise attached to the commands, not just a pile of rules. Friends, that's a great deal.

The missing word is test. Moses says the LORD led them “…so that He might humble you and test you in order to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep His commandments.” (Deuteronomy 8:2) A test brings out what's really in there. I think that's like pulling a tray out of the oven to see how the dough actually turned out.

The answer is manna. In their hunger, the LORD gave Israel manna to eat, which neither they nor their fathers had known. Picture waking up hungry and breakfast is something nobody in your family has ever seen before. That's a morning nobody forgets.

The answer is every word from the mouth of the LORD. Moses says the manna was so they might understand that man does not live on bread alone, “…but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.” (Deuteronomy 8:3) Jesus answers the tempter with this teaching in the wilderness (Matthew 4:4). Bread keeps you going for a day, friends, and the LORD's word is what you really live on.

The answer is True. Moses says it plainly: “Your clothing did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.” (Deuteronomy 8:4) Forty years of walking, and the clothes held up. Friends, I've seen an apron give up after one batch of cinnamon dough.

The missing word is son. Moses says, “…just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.” (Deuteronomy 8:5) Notice who he picks: a father and his son. Not a boss and a worker. Proverbs says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as a father disciplines the son in whom he delights. (Proverbs 3:12)

The answer is brooks and fountains and springs. Moses calls it “…a land of brooks and fountains and springs that flow through the valleys and hills…” (Deuteronomy 8:7) That's three kinds of water in one breath. After a wilderness described as thirsty and waterless, I think that sounds mighty fine.

The answer is that they will eat without any scarcity. Moses says it's “…a land where you will eat food without scarcity, where you will lack nothing…” (Deuteronomy 8:9) Lack nothing, friends. I've never once finished a batch and still had enough cookies.

The answer is False. Moses names iron and copper: “a land whose rocks are iron and whose hills are ready to be mined for copper.” (Deuteronomy 8:9) Gold does come up later, in verse 13, but as wealth that increases. This verse is about the ground, and the ground gives iron and copper.

The answer is to bless the LORD for the land. Moses says, “When you eat and are satisfied, you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.” (Deuteronomy 8:10) The moment he names is a full stomach. I'd say that's a habit that fits any kitchen, even mine after a big batch.

The answer is when they are full and rich and settled. Moses warns, “Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses in which to dwell, and when your herds and flocks grow large…” (Deuteronomy 8:12-13) Forgetting doesn't always show up with trouble, friends. Sometimes it shows up with a nice house and a full pantry.

The missing word is proud. Moses says, “…then your heart will become proud, and you will forget the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” (Deuteronomy 8:14) Pride and forgetting go hand in hand there. A full house can leave less room for remembering.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD their God is the One “…who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” (Deuteronomy 8:14) He puts that memory right next to the warning about forgetting. It's the very thing he doesn't want lost.

The answer is the rock of flint. Moses says, “He brought you water from the rock of flint.” (Deuteronomy 8:15) A rock, friends. Most folks wouldn't walk up to a rock and ask it for a drink. That's what makes this one stand out.

The missing word is prosper. Moses says the humbling and testing were “…so that in the end He might cause you to prosper.” (Deuteronomy 8:16) The hard stretch had an end in view, and that end was prospering. Forty years is a long road, so I think those two words, “…in the end…” matter.

The answer is that their own strength made this wealth. Moses says Israel might say in their heart, “The power and strength of my hands have made this wealth for me.” (Deuteronomy 8:17) That's the thought where you hand yourself the trophy. Right after, Moses steers them back to who really gives the power.

The answer is False. Moses says, “…it is the LORD your God who gives you the power to gain wealth…” (Deuteronomy 8:18) So the power comes from the LORD, not from the land. I like a good rich piece of ground, friends, but it doesn't get the credit here.

The answer is to confirm His covenant with their fathers. Moses says the LORD gives the power to gain wealth “…in order to confirm His covenant that He swore to your fathers even to this day.” (Deuteronomy 8:18) It ties back to what He swore long ago. The wealth isn't random, and it isn't a trophy for them.

The answer is that they will surely perish. This is a heavy one, friends. Moses says, “…I testify against you today that you will surely perish.” (Deuteronomy 8:19) He says it about forgetting the LORD and going after other gods to worship and bow down to them. He's serious because the stakes are serious.

The answer is the nations the LORD destroyed before them. Moses says, “Like the nations that the LORD has destroyed before you, so you will perish if you do not obey the LORD your God.” (Deuteronomy 8:20) It's a sober comparison, and he means it. I think he wants Israel to hear it clearly.
